Kernel `bv_neg_radius` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: the oracle tests it, but Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

$r_x$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$r_z = \mathrm{RN}(r_x).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Target (not proved)

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r_z = \mathrm{RN}(r_x)$: the number of the format nearest to $r_x$, ties to even.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked.

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bv_neg_radius_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m rx : R,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  let rz := bv_neg_radius m rx in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  rz = RN emin prec rx.
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius of ball_neg_k (Milestone 1 listing), at every entry (milestone2.md, BallVector). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_neg_radius.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_neg_radius.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The one radius of the negation of a BallVector (milestone2.md, "BallVector": bv_neg_k): the radius of
# the operand, unchanged, as ball_neg_k returns it entry by entry. The negation of a center is exact,
# so nothing is added: the result is exactly the set of the negated members. The largest magnitude of
# a center, which every radius kernel of a ball vector takes, is not needed: a canonical operand has
# finite centers or zero ones, and so has its negation.

rz = copy(rx)
```
